subject.title: [Security] Missing complexity validation and rate limiting on log query filters

question: Should repeated loadSession replay by an already-known ACP client receive a separate per-client work budget, or is ACP's local/operator-controlled trust boundary sufficient once the nonexistent recursive-filter claim is dismissed?
rationale: Source inspection disproves the reported arbitrary-filter path, but deciding whether repeated authenticated replay is an abuse boundary requires maintainer security intent and an acceptable reconnect policy.

options.title: Benchmark then budget replay
options.body: Measure maximum-size repeated replay and add a narrow limiter or work budget only if it can materially stall the process.

options.title: Accept the ACP trust boundary
options.body: Document that ACP clients are operator-controlled and close the report if repeated bounded replay is not treated as an adversarial surface.

options.title: Rate-limit every replay
options.body: Apply a strict limiter to all loadSession calls, accepting possible reconnect and IDE usability regressions.

recommendation.title: Benchmark then budget replay
recommendation.body: Measure maximum-size repeated replay and add a narrow limiter or work budget only if it can materially stall the process.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue timeline explicitly routed the security-boundary question to this reviewer after initial source triage.
